page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical ARMv9 cores using the AWS Neoverse-V2 (Graviton) processor running at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity sits at 32.0 GB, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance includes a 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and delivers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no GPUs attached.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in memory-bound and multi-core operations. The instance achieved top-tier performance on the PassMark memory test (3138.89), alongside top 25% marks in uncached large block read (296.81 GB/sec) and write (124.13 GB/sec) memory bandwidth. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15891.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 203.34 GB/sec. Compute-focused PassMark database operations also tested in the top 25% with 23981.75. Standard compute benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1891.0) and stress-ng multi-core (27304.24) fall in the middle 50% category.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with high memory bandwidth and local NVMe SSD storage makes the c8gd.4xlarge cost-efficient for core-dense applications requiring fast ephemeral storage. While medium-model LLM prompt processing shows lower efficiency (bottom 25% at 31.26 tokens/sec), the configuration is well aligned with workloads such as CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, distributed compilation, and database engines requiring fast local caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and 16 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), a direct-attached 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, it displays top-tier memory scores and strong uncached read/write memory bandwidth, as well as top 25% scores in multi-core Geekbench execution and database operations. General compute tasks, Clang compilation, and single-threaded operations perform in the average middle tier. The lack of simultaneous multithreading provides consistent single-threaded execution per vCPU. This instance configuration is suitable for distributed compilation, high-throughput caching databases, batch processing, and continuous integration pipelines.
